$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package devkit. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-SHARE-WHOLE
arms.note: the suite's shards and the arms' jobs take the whole lease beside the rows already holding threads, so the slice gate oversubscribes the lease it runs under

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-FOREIGN-REPORT
arms.note: a report an earlier run's orphaned branch left under the same name is read as this run's, so a branch that died without reporting shows the old run's verdict

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-LIGHT-NONE
arms.note: the light branches hold nothing in the reckoning, so the heavy branch asks the pool for the whole budget beside the leases the lint and the probes take, and the gate's branches oversubscribe the machine

arms.name: M-LEASE-NEST-UNDER-HELD
arms.note: a run under its caller's lease asks the pool for more, so a waiter queued ahead of it for the threads it holds waits for ever

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-LIGHT-NOT-AHEAD
arms.note: the light branches queue at the heavy one's priority, so on a busy pool the heavy one's whole-share wait closes the free threads to its own siblings and the lint and the probes wait for the pool to drain

arms.name: M-COMMAND-SHORT-DRIVEN
arms.note: every git the tools run starts a node process driver first, so the gate's git-heavy classes pay a node start per call

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-HEAVY-NOT-SPLIT
arms.note: each heavy branch of a gate asks for the whole rest of the lease, so the suite and the base suite beside it oversubscribe the threads the lease holds

arms.name: M-LEASE-EST-EMITTED
arms.note: a flexible lease never tells the pool its per-size estimate, so the pool picks the size by waiting for the whole share

arms.name: M-LEASE-EST-ONLY-WITH-CURVE
arms.note: a lease whose curve holds a size without a time still sends the flag, which the pool refuses with exit 64 and no lease

arms.name: M-LEASE-EST-NONE-WITHOUT-CURVE
arms.find: if (seconds == null || ask.min >= ask.max) return null;
arms.note: a lease with no curve still sends an empty flag, which the pool refuses with exit 64 and no lease

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-HEAVY-ASK-CURVE
arms.note: the ask never carries the curve the history knows, so no flag reaches the pool

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-HISTORY-ASK
arms.note: the heavy branch never reads its history, so the pool keeps waiting for its whole share

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-RECORD-FIT
arms.note: a branch with a failed step records its time, and a red run that stopped early reads as the branch's speed

arms.name: M-BOUNDEDLOG-BOUND
arms.note: a bounded line file is never compacted, so the history and the ledger grow with every run

arms.name: M-LEASEHISTORY-FIT-FILL
arms.note: the sizes never run take no time in the curve, so the pool picks the largest size whatever the measured ones say

arms.name: M-LEASEHISTORY-KEY
arms.note: a label keeps its slice id and commit, so no two runs share a key and no history ever builds

arms.name: M-LEASEHISTORY-MIN-RUNS
arms.note: a size run once or twice takes that run as its time, so one slow run sets the estimate the pool picks a size by

arms.name: M-LEASEHISTORY-ONE-SIZE-NO-CURVE
arms.note: one measured size fits a flat curve through the whole range, so the pool is told every size takes as long as the one that was run

arms.name: M-LEASEHISTORY-RECENT
arms.note: every run ever recorded counts, so a tree that got faster is estimated by the runs of the tree it was

arms.name: M-LEASEHISTORY-SERIES-BOUND
arms.note: a compaction keeps every run of a series, so one command run often fills the file with its own past

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-READINGS-WRITTEN
arms.note: a row's cpu seconds are dropped from its line, so the ledger shows a row with no cpu reading whatever its process used

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-BOUND
arms.note: the file never compacts, so a ledger appended to by every run grows without bound

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-NO-WALL-SKIPPED
arms.note: a line whose wall time is no number reads back as a row with a NaN wall time

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-NO-NAME-RECORDED
arms.note: a row with no name is appended, and its line names no row on the next read

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-TAB-IN-NAME
arms.note: a tab in a row's name splits its line into more fields, so every reading after it shifts one field

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-READINGS-ENCODED
arms.note: a step's cpu seconds never reach its branch's report, so the parent's summary shows none however much a branch measured

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-WAIT-FIRST-STEP
arms.note: every row of a waiting branch carries its lease wait, so the table shows the same wait on each of them

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-CPU-FIRST-STEP
arms.replace: if (used != null) for (name in names) cpus[name] = used;
arms.note: every row of a metered branch carries the whole branch cpu, so a ledger summing rows counts it once per row

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-CPU-STALE
arms.note: a usage file an earlier run left is read as this branch cpu

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-METERED-OFF
arms.note: the branch runs without time(1), so no step carries cpu

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-CPU-COMMA
arms.note: a time(1) report in a comma locale reads 2,99 as 2

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-OFSTEPS-BRANCH
arms.note: a gate step after its branch first names no branch, so the ledger sums it apart from the cpu its branch used

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-GATE-BRANCHES
arms.note: a gate step is filed under the last earlier step with a lease instead of its real branch, so a corpus row counts under lists

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-BATTERY-TWICE
arms.note: the land battery step keeps its whole wall beside the battery rows, so a sum over the ledger counts the battery twice

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-LAND-DROPS-BATTERY
arms.note: a land records only its own rows, so the battery rows its child wrote never reach the shared ledger

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-OFBATTERY-GATE
arms.note: a land that takes a gate record over leaves that gate's rows out of the ledger, so dev exec-ledger under-counts every reused land

arms.name: M-CPUMETER-READS-USAGE
arms.note: the usage file of an ended process is read and thrown away, so a step that ran work reads zero cpu

arms.name: M-CPUMETER-WRAP-OFF
arms.note: a job is handed to time(1) with its arguments but still starts the program itself, so no process runs under the meter

arms.name: M-CPUMETER-WRAPS-MEASURED
arms.note: a branch already under time(1) is wrapped a second time, and the meter counts its cpu again

arms.name: M-CPUMETER-SHORT-BOUND
arms.note: a short program under the meter loses the bound it would have had in this process, so a wedged git is never killed

arms.name: M-COMMAND-RUNS-METERED
arms.note: a command a tool runs is started as it is, so a metered run's steps measure none of the processes they start

arms.name: M-SUMMARY-STEP-CPU
arms.note: a timed step records no cpu of the processes it started, so a land's phases show as unmetered

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-OVERHEAD-CPU-TWICE
arms.note: the land's battery step keeps its whole cpu beside the battery's span, so a sum over the ledger counts the battery's cpu twice

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-SPAN-CPU
arms.note: the battery's span row carries no cpu, so the whole battery shows as unmetered beside its metered branches

arms.name: M-CPUMETER-RUNNING-READ-ZERO
arms.note: a process still running (its usage file opened and not yet filled) is dropped from the meter, so its cpu is lost

arms.name: M-CPUMETER-BEGIN-KEEPS-STRAYS
arms.note: a usage file an earlier attempt left under a name this run reuses is read as this run's cpu

arms.name: M-LEASE-CORES-IGNORED
arms.note: an ask whose processes each run on several cpus still leases one thread per process, so a node engine runs on more cpus than its lease holds

arms.name: M-LEASE-CORES-UNCAPPED
arms.note: a scaled ask can name more threads than the pool has, so the lease waits for a grant that never comes

arms.name: M-LEASE-CORES-CPUS-TO-COMMAND
arms.note: a command leased by the cpu reads the cpus as its process count, so its compiler fan-out doubles and overruns the lease it was scaled to fit

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-CORES-UNASKED
arms.note: a light branch of node engine processes leases one thread per process, so the gate lint runs on more cpus than it holds

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-HEAVY-BESIDE-THREADS
arms.note: the heavy branch is sized beside the light ones processes, not the cpus they lease, so together they ask for more than the budget

arms.name: M-LEASE-CORES-PRIORITY-DROPPED
arms.note: a scaled ask loses its priority, so the gate lint queues behind the heavy branch's whole-share wait

arms.name: M-LEASE-CORES-UNGUARDED
arms.note: a command with no grant is handed one process in WF_THREADS, so a caller outside any lease reads a lease it never took

arms.name: M-CPUMETER-SINCE-LOST
arms.note: a span in which a process left no usage reads the cpu of the rest, a figure too low to be a reading

arms.name: M-SUMMARY-STEP-THREADS
arms.note: a step that reported the pool threads it held records none, so the ledger cannot say what its cpu was spent against

arms.name: M-SUMMARY-HELD-STALE
arms.note: the threads one step reported stand on the next step that reports none

arms.name: M-BRANCHES-UNLISTED-DROPPED
arms.note: a branch that is no line of the table (the base lint beside the gate) holds a lease the ledger never sees

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-BASE-TWICE
arms.note: the land's base step keeps the cpu of the snapshot battery it ran, which that battery's rows record again

arms.name: M-EXECLEDGER-LAND-DROPS-SNAPSHOT
arms.note: the rows of the snapshot battery a land ran are recorded nowhere, so the threads that battery held are unread

arms.name: M-LEASE-THREADS-OF-CORES
arms.note: a lease taker that runs a process on several cpus is recorded as holding one thread per process, not the cpus it leased
